fixes.explanation: Harvest does show up in this passage, friend, but later. Gathering from the threshing floor and the winepress goes with the Feast of Tabernacles (Deuteronomy 16:13). Moses ties the month of Abib to something else: the LORD bringing Israel out of Egypt (Deuteronomy 16:1). Right passage, different feast.

Not quite, friend. Moses says the LORD brought Israel out of Egypt “by night.” (Deuteronomy 16:1) Daylight isn't in the verse at all. So the night is the part to hold onto, and I'd say that's one to circle in your Bible with a big marker.

Yes, baker. Moses says to offer the Passover sacrifice “…in the place the LORD will choose as a dwelling for His Name.” (Deuteronomy 16:2) Israel doesn't pick the spot. The LORD does. Moses says it again in verse 6, so you get to hear it twice.

Regret is a heavy word, friend, and Moses doesn't hand it out here. He says the bread is so they “…may remember for the rest of your life the day you left the land of Egypt.” (Deuteronomy 16:3) He even calls it “the bread of affliction” and says they left in haste. The point of the bread is remembering that day, every year, for life.

Mourning isn't the word, baker. Moses says, “…you shall rejoice before the LORD your God…” (Deuteronomy 16:11) And look who's invited: sons, daughters, servants, the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless and the widows. That's a full table, and the instruction for all of them is to rejoice.

This one is true, baker. Moses says, “Remember that you were slaves in Egypt, and carefully follow these statutes.” (Deuteronomy 16:12) That's the memory he wants them holding onto. And right with it comes the call to follow the statutes carefully.

Abib is the month Moses names back at the start of the passage, baker. It goes with the Passover and the LORD bringing Israel out of Egypt (Deuteronomy 16:1). For the Feast of Tabernacles, Moses gives a different marker: after they've gathered from the threshing floor and the winepress (Deuteronomy 16:13). So look for the gathering, not the month.

That's the reason, friend. Moses says, “…because the LORD your God will bless you in all your produce and in all the work of your hands, so that your joy will be complete.” (Deuteronomy 16:15) Think about that: all the work of your hands, and the LORD is the one doing the blessing. I'd throw a seven-day feast for that too, and I'd bring the cookies.
